bug_semantics: An authenticated Administration Console user can persist attacker-controlled text in a configuration attribute, demonstrated by an application's description. A later browser request for that configuration object through the management REST interface receives text/html. The HTML provider reads the stored ConfigBean attribute and inserts it into generated markup without contextual HTML encoding; the reported payload containing is consequently parsed as an element and executes in the Administration Console origin with the victim administrator's session.
flaw_origin: Legacy GlassFish commit be6b1571814721625e5e70343a2b178076d61450 first added the REST management HTML provider and directly concatenated proxy.attribute(attribute) between h2 tags. That was already an executable stored-XSS sink for attacker-controlled persistent configuration values. Commit 881906985072f3326ed2a53d3aa2f07a2c0973f8 later changed the presentation context to an unencoded input value attribute but did not introduce the underlying browser-facing unencoded output. Later provider moves, renames, refactors, and the parentless Eclipse Initial Contribution aggregate preserved the flaw and are rejected as BICs.
ai_marker: absent: git cat-file -p and git show -s of the BIC identify human author and committer Ludovic Champenois <ludo@java.net>, dated 2009-04-20T18:37:17+00:00. The complete commit message contains a normal feature description, SVN revision 26425, and Former-commit-id metadata, with no AI assistant, bot identity, Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, or other AI-attribution marker.
evidence: The assigned advisory bundle identifies CVE-2024-9343 / GHSA-mqxx-c43h-jj9v as stored XSS in the GlassFish Administration Console, package org.glassfish.main.admingui:console-common, affected range <= 7.0.25, and no first patched version.

The disputed introducer_sha is resolved in favor of the reviewer. git log -S 'proxy.attribute(attribute)' be6b1571814721625e5e70343a2b178076d61450 -- v3/admin/rest/src/main/java/org/glassfish/admin/rest/provider/SingletonDomHtmlProvider.java returns only be6b1571814721625e5e70343a2b178076d61450. git log -L 119,130 on that file shows the file's /dev/null addition, including result concatenation of attribute, ':' and proxy.attribute(attribute) between h2 tags. Because arbitrary persistent attribute text containing an img/onerror element already becomes active text/html, this is the same stored-XSS mechanism before the later value-attribute layout.

The disputed introducer_parent is likewise resolved in favor of the reviewer. The BIC commit object names immediate parent ca915d3d98df6c4091499968f9b64eb3f8af9783. git ls-tree -r --name-only of that parent for SingletonDomHtmlProvider.java prints nothing, while git diff-tree --name-status of the BIC reports the file as A; the direct parent therefore lacks the provider and vulnerable sink.

The primary candidate 881906985072f3326ed2a53d3aa2f07a2c0973f8 is rejected. git grep at its parent bc3bc2bffef6c015dc3e6252b3fea9cb73447d7e finds proxy.attribute(attribute) already emitted by GetResultHtmlProvider.java, and the candidate's diff removes that raw display from GetResultHtmlProvider while adding getHtmlRespresentationForAttributes in ProviderUtil with the same raw value in an input attribute. It changes HTML context and adds browser editing; it does not start the unencoded-output vulnerability.

git log --follow through GetResultHtmlProvider.java at 881906985072f3326ed2a53d3aa2f07a2c0973f8 reaches be6b1571814721625e5e70343a2b178076d61450 as the earliest entry, demonstrating the provider lineage rather than treating later renames or moves as introductions. The current repository's history begins at parentless commit 571714739b23e16c4c90d5229b806433920b3bcb ('Initial Contribution'); that aggregate is rejected, and the surviving sink is decomposed to the legacy source commit.

Version-boundary checks resolve tags 7.0.15, 7.0.25, and 7.0.26 to 6f2f4c26b0f825d36b45ef39f6f83ac6b56d438c, 17c9f164606e47efbc58907a97ad351a7f54089e, and 215b00392179abfef69725ff07455096f2e7fa19 respectively. git grep -n 'append(parameterValue)' at all three tags and HEAD finds the unencoded input value sink in ProviderUtil.java. Audited HEAD 4a143866f4a92995e6387ee33f5412bdeac38567 still retains it, so there is no public fix commit or patched boundary to record.

git cat-file -p be6b1571814721625e5e70343a2b178076d61450 verifies parent ca915d3d98df6c4091499968f9b64eb3f8af9783 and the complete BIC commit object. Its human author/committer and message contain no AI attribution signal, so the BIC-only attribution rule yields NOT_AI.
reasoning: The audits disagreed because the primary treated the later quoted-input rendering as the first relevant sink, whereas the reviewer traced the vulnerability at the correct semantic level: persistent attacker-controlled configuration data rendered into text/html without output encoding. The reviewer's be6b1571814721625e5e70343a2b178076d61450 wins both assigned fields. It is the smallest source commit that created a text/html provider and emitted proxy.attribute(attribute) raw; the reported img/onerror payload is executable in that original element-content context as well. Its immediate parent ca915d3d98df6c4091499968f9b64eb3f8af9783 lacks the provider. The primary's 881906985072f3326ed2a53d3aa2f07a2c0973f8 merely relocates an already-vulnerable raw value from display content to an editable value attribute, so selecting it would incorrectly make a presentation rewrite the BIC. The legacy source commit also precedes the affected 7.x lineage, while the sink persists through the advisory boundary and current HEAD. Finally, only the resolved BIC commit object is used for attribution, and it supplies no AI signal; the gate-complete outcome is NOT_AI with justified null fix fields because the case remains unpatched.
remaining_gap: No upstream fix or first patched version is published or present in the audited history: the vulnerable interpolation remains in 7.0.26 and audited HEAD 4a143866f4a92995e6387ee33f5412bdeac38567, so fix_sha and direct_fix_sha are intentionally null.
